title: Scalar-unit coefficient square for derived direct image
statement:
Let $f:\mathscr X\to\mathscr Y$ be a morphism of topoi presented by small sites [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A\xrightarrow{a}R\xrightarrow{c}S$ be maps of sheaves of commutative rings on $\mathscr Y$, and on $\mathscr X$ use their inverse images $A_X,R_X,S_X$ with the induced maps. Use ordinary unbounded derived module categories, K-flat derived scalar extension and K-injective right derived direct image [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Write $G_D=Rf_{*,D}$ for $D=A,R,S$, with the canonical derived adjunctions [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. For $V\in D(A_X)$ put $V_R=R_X\otimes_{A_X}^LV$ and $V_S=S_X\otimes_{A_X}^LV$.

Let $\beta_R:R\otimes_A^LG_AV\to G_RV_R$ be the transpose under derived extension/restriction of the composite of $G_A$ applied to the scalar unit $V\to\operatorname{Res}_aV_R$ with the canonical derived comparison with exact restriction; define $\beta_S$ similarly for $ca$. Define $m:V_R\to\operatorname{Res}_{c_X}V_S$ and $\gamma:R\otimes_A^LG_AV\to\operatorname{Res}_c(S\otimes_A^LG_AV)$ by $z\otimes v\mapsto c(z)\otimes v$ on K-flat models. Let $\kappa:G_RV_R\to\operatorname{Res}_cG_SV_S$ be $G_R(m)$ followed by the canonical comparison with exact restriction. Then
$$\operatorname{Res}_c(\beta_S)\circ\gamma=\kappa\circ\beta_R$$
in $D(R)$. The equality and all these transformations are natural in $V$ and commute with the canonical integer shifts. The equality remains true after restriction to $A$, and is carried to the same specified maps by any exact equivalences compatible with these scalar adjunction units, counits, restriction comparisons and shifts. No invertibility of a projection, flatness of a coefficient map, or boundedness of $V$ is assumed.

proof.text:
Write $U_a,U_c,U_{ca}$ for derived restriction on $\mathscr Y$ and $U_{a,X},U_{c,X},U_{ca,X}$ on $\mathscr X$. Restriction is exact by the sheaf-ring coefficient-adjunction theorem. Regard each coefficient map as the identity-topos ringed morphism, whose right derived direct image is therefore this termwise restriction. The two ringed factorizations from $(\mathscr X,R_X)$ to $(\mathscr Y,A)$ have identical geometric morphism and structural map. The ringed composition and two-isomorphism comparisons give the specified natural isomorphism $\theta_a:G_AU_{a,X}\cong U_aG_R$; similarly obtain $\theta_c,\theta_{ca}$. Their normalizations are those of the canonical comparisons in the statement, by the K-injective-normalized direct-image composition theorem. For the three-ring diagram these satisfy
$$\theta_{ca}=U_a(\theta_c)\circ\theta_aU_{c,X}.$$
Indeed take adjunction mates. Each path on left adjoints is ordinary pullback and tensor reassociation on flat-term K-flat representatives; both send $s\otimes r\otimes x$ to $s c(r)\otimes x$. These maps agree before localization, so the normalized left comparisons agree. Composite adjunction Hom bijections are composites of bijections, hence their corresponding right comparisons agree as well. This proves the equation for the specified comparisons; it does not assume that restriction preserves K-injectives.

proof.text:
For any $Q\in D(A)$ write $\eta_a(Q):Q\to U_a(R\otimes_A^LQ)$ and $\eta_{ca}(Q):Q\to U_{ca}(S\otimes_A^LQ)$ for scalar units. The normalized coefficient adjunction computes them by $x\mapsto1\otimes x$ on one flat-term K-flat representative $P$ of $Q$. The maps $\gamma_Q$ and $m$ are induced on this same representative by $r\otimes x\mapsto c(r)\otimes x$. Thus
$$U_a(\gamma_Q)\eta_a(Q)=\eta_{ca}(Q),\qquad U_{a,X}(m)\eta_a(V)=\eta_{ca}(V).$$
Each equality is the chain-map equality $x\mapsto1\otimes x$, since $c(1)=1$. K-flat computation and the normalized unit formulas carry it to the derived category. The same formulas commute with maps of representatives and hence define natural transformations. No tensoring of an arbitrary quasi-isomorphism by a nonflat ring is used.

proof.text:
Put $Q=G_AV$. By definition of transpose, the $a$-adjunct of $\beta_R$ is $t_R=\theta_aG_A(\eta_a(V))$, and the $ca$-adjunct of $\beta_S$ is $t_S=\theta_{ca}G_A(\eta_{ca}(V))$. Take the $a$-adjunct of the left side of the desired equality, whose target is $U_cG_SV_S$. It is
$$U_{ca}(\beta_S)\,U_a(\gamma_Q)\,\eta_a(Q)
=U_{ca}(\beta_S)\eta_{ca}(Q)=t_S.$$
The first equality is Step 2, the second is the defining adjunct identity for $\beta_S$. The formula for an adjunct is restriction followed by precomposition with the unit, so this computation occurs in $D(A)$, without asserting that restriction alone is faithful on derived morphisms.

source.place: Tags 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition), 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition), 0FPI (lemma-adjoints-push-pull-compatibility); scalar-unit calculation refining blueprint direct-images proof paragraph (3).

proof.text:
The $a$-adjunct of the right side is
$$U_a(\theta_c)\,U_aG_R(m)\,t_R
=U_a(\theta_c)\,\theta_a(U_{c,X}V_S)\,G_A(U_{a,X}(m))\,G_A(\eta_a(V))
=\theta_{ca}G_A(\eta_{ca}(V))=t_S.$$
Here the first equality uses naturality of $\theta_a$ for the morphism $m:V_R\to U_{c,X}V_S$; the second uses the comparison equation of Step 1, the scalar-unit equation of Step 2, and functoriality of $G_A$. Both sides therefore have the same adjunct by Step 3. Injectivity of the scalar-adjunction Hom bijection proves the requested equality in $D(R)$, which is stronger than merely proving its restriction.

proof.text: Naturality in $V$ follows from naturality of scalar units, the $\theta$ comparisons, and the adjunction Hom bijections: the adjunct of the naturality square for $\beta_R$ is the naturality square for $\theta_aG_A\eta_a$, and likewise for $S$. For shifts, the canonical ringed derived adjunction theorem says that units and counits commute with every integer shift. This applies also to identity-topos coefficient morphisms, identifying their units with the normalized scalar units. The maps $m,\gamma$ commute with shift on complexes: $c(r)\otimes x$ has the same degree as $r\otimes x$, and both differentials gain the same $(-1)^n$. The $\theta$ comparisons commute with shift as well: shift the K-injective representatives and the resolution maps in their normalized composition formulas. They remain such representatives and resolutions by K-injective shift stability, and ordinary direct image and restriction commute termwise with shift. Naturality of the resolution identifications gives the canonical comparison at the shifted input. Finally, transpose the shift square for $\beta_R$. Unit-shift compatibility identifies its two adjuncts with the shift square for $\theta_aG_A\eta_a$, already proved; injectivity proves the square for $\beta_R$, and identically for $\beta_S$. Thus every specified map and the equality respect the canonical integer shifts.

proof.text:
Apply the functor $U_a$ to the equality in $D(R)$ to obtain its asserted restriction to $A$. For the equivalence clause, denote the supplied comparison isomorphisms at the source and target of any arrow $h$ by $e_0,e_1$. Its transported arrow is $e_1E(h)e_0^{-1}$. For composable $h,k$ the transported composite is
$$e_2E(kh)e_0^{-1}=(e_2E(k)e_1^{-1})(e_1E(h)e_0^{-1}),$$
by functoriality and $e_1^{-1}e_1=1$. Unit and restriction compatibility identify the transported $m,\gamma$ with their specified maps: their scalar adjuncts are the specified units of Step 2, which determine them uniquely. Compatibility with adjunction units and counits identifies the transported adjunct of $\beta_R$ with $\theta_aG_A\eta_a$, so uniqueness of adjuncts identifies the transported $\beta_R$ with the specified one; likewise for $S$. Restriction-comparison compatibility identifies $\kappa$ with $G_R(m)$ followed by the specified comparison. Applying the displayed composite formula now gives exactly the specified square after transport. The assumed shift compatibility carries all the shift squares of Step 5 with it.
